full_script: Who could fall for some silly scam like the Nigerian prince fraud? Well, actually, some Nigerian politicians. When advance-fee email scams exploded, causing nearly a billion dollars in losses, the government launched an anti-corruption commission to hunt the fraudsters. However, this completely backfired. Scammers did something genius. Instead of targeting random foreigners, they posed as federal investigators and sent letters to corrupt politicians. They told the politicians they had proof of their illegal bribes, but would kill the investigation for a fee. Out of pure paranoia, guilty officials rushed to comply. Raking in millions of dollars by using the politicians' own guilty secrets against them.
